lineas.texto: In La Paz, Bolivia, beans can boil for hours and stay hard.
The city is over three and a half kilometers up, so less air presses down on the water.
With less pressure, water boils at about eighty eight degrees, not one hundred.
It bubbles like crazy, but it never gets hotter than that.
That's why so many kitchens up there have a pressure cooker.
The lid seals in the steam, and the pressure climbs.
Now the water can't boil until it's well past one hundred degrees.
Hotter water, and hours of cooking turn into minutes.
